topics.topic: Whether both Registry surfaces must be served in an owner-only start
questions: Does the statement that Registry serves two surfaces describe only the full-start capability, with an owner-only start serving one surface, or does it require every running process to serve both surfaces?
Is “serving two surfaces” a statement of available surface types, or an invariant that both surfaces are served in every running instance?

quotes:
The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the configured addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
judgement.why: The module text expressly says that an owner-only start opens the owner interface alone, so “two surfaces” describes the available surface types rather than an invariant that both are always open.

topics.topic: How configuration performs final listener checks despite later-module dependencies
questions: How can A17's primary owner `configuration` own or perform the required final listener-opening checks when `service_api`, `owner_interface` and `instance_lifecycle` are later modules that it may not know?

topics.topic: Module ownership and lifecycle of service and owner-interface listeners
questions: Which module owns creating, configuring, exclusively binding, closing and attaching a handler to each listener, and which module decides that the service-API listener is absent in an owner-only start?

judgement.why: This asks the same listener-ownership and startup-coordination question already answered by P2, and the relevant module passages have not changed.

precedent.topic: Module ownership and enforcement of listener socket policy and socket creation
quotes: Ownership is by rule, not by decision: a consumer owns exactly the rules and parts of the decision its own section below names, and the primary owner owns every rule of the decision that no other section names, except a rule this text places outside the running instance (A20, A21, A22 rule 6's "never declared again"), which no module owns.

The checks after them — the backup probe (`backups`), opening or making the store (`store`) and the listeners — are run in rule 2's order by
`instance_lifecycle`, which calls this module first.

The start and the running instance: `configuration` first, then the backup
probe and `store`, then the listeners at the configured addresses, serving
nothing until every check passed and having `store` remove a store this start
made new when a listener cannot be opened (A17 rule 2); the
owner-only start, which opens the owner interface alone (A17 rule 1, A18
rule 9); the two surfaces, the owner interface's listener opened first; the 60-second pass
of `owner_sessions` and the minute look of `backups` (A13 rule 2, A18 rule 1);
that a restart ends every owner session (A13 rule 2).
precedent.why: The ownership rule assigns otherwise-unnamed A17 policy to primary owner `configuration`, while `instance_lifecycle` owns and performs the expressly named listener-opening mechanism.

topics.topic: Who initializes M12 AuditSequence when a database is created
questions: Who supplies the rule and operation that creates M12 at zero while `store` makes a new database, given that `store` is earlier than `audit_log` and may not know it?

quotes:
The one SQLite database (L19) and its connections — the one the
transactions of actions run on, and the read connection a backup's copy
takes its snapshot on while they go on, under the engine setting State 6
fixes, the snapshot fixed by its first read, of the audit counter, with the
clock read then (A18 rule 1): opening it for reading and
writing at start, or making a new, empty store of the release's version —
holding no record but M12 AuditSequence at 0, which the release's statements
make with the store, so `store` needs nothing from `audit_log` — under
the temporary name and renaming it once complete, after removing a leftover of
that name and no other file (A17 rule 5), and removing a store it made new
when the start then fails at a listener (A17 rule 2); the full integrity check —
`PRAGMA integrity_check` answering `ok`, `PRAGMA foreign_key_check` finding
nothing — and the store version check (A17 rule 5), the same check `backups`
asks of a backup's copy.
judgement.why: The unchanged `store` passage already assigns construction of the release-defined initial M12 record to `store` without a dependency on `audit_log`, and the reopening change did not touch or make this ownership matter.
